text.p: - The poor ventilation system in the Moscow underground, designed 60 years ago, could spell disaster for people prone to respiratory diseases this winter.
- Thousands of Russian servicemen are still waiting for decent housing as the German houses-for-troops-withdrawal aid programme nears its completion.
- Sergei Leonyuk, newly-appointed head of the controversial National Sports Fund, joins the campaign of intensive mud slinging between top Russian officials.
- Russian President Boris Yeltsin, in a sanatorium preparing for heart surgery, seems to be the most calm among Russian politicians and firmly in control of the situation.
- President Yeltsin will shortly sign a decree seriously curbing powers of the country's natural monopolies.
- The Moscow government plans to start placing its own bonds in December.

- The trumpeted introduction of new Russian passports to replace the anachronistic but still valid red hammer-and-sickle identity papers could be of no consequence as no official state emblem or coat of arms have been passed in the new Russia.
- The prosecutor general's office is carry out thorough checks at the Finance ministry to investigate where budget money goes.
- The paper repeats its allegations that a high-ranking Central Bank official sold confidential information to a commercial bank and may have played a part in the rouble collapse in October 1994.
